plain_description.what: Simulating sending questions to the wrong cell (10, 19 and 30% error, plus the tree's real 24.7% mismatch with declared subjects). It measures how much this weakens per-cell model differences, across 168 subject-by-model cells.
plain_description.why: Per-cell routing is only useful if realistic misrouting does not wash out the differences it is meant to reveal.
plain_description.information: Result (no new calls): the criterion fails. At 19% misrouting, 42 of 168 cell differences shift by more than their standard error. The effect is a uniform shrinkage (about 20% at 19%). It hurts most where differences are large, not in the small subjects, which pass only because their uncertainty is larger. No established model ordering was reversed under any misrouting level.
